questions.q: Using the displayed firm graph, what market price does the competitive firm take as given?
questions.feedback: The horizontal P = MR = AR line is at $30.

questions.q: Where does the $30 MR line meet rising MC, identifying the profit-maximizing quantity?
options: 20 units
50 units
30 units
70 units
questions.feedback: The relevant rising MC curve meets P = MR at Q = 50.

questions.q: At the profit-maximizing output, what is average total cost?
questions.feedback: At Q = 50, the ATC guide is $20.

questions.q: At Q = 50, what is average variable cost on the displayed graph?
questions.feedback: The AVC guide at Q = 50 is $10.

questions.q: At the 50-unit output in the displayed competitive-market graph, what vertical price–ATC gap represents profit on each unit?
options: $10 per unit
$20 per unit
$30 per unit
$40 per unit
questions.feedback: Profit per unit is P − ATC = $30 − $20 = $10.

questions.q: What is total economic profit at the displayed profit-maximizing output?
questions.feedback: Total profit is ($30 − $20) × 50 = $500.

questions.q: Using the firm’s profit-maximizing output and the market price shown, calculate total revenue.
Using the displayed ATC at the profit-maximizing output, calculate the firm’s total cost.
Using ATC and AVC at Q = 50, what total fixed cost is implied by the graph?
Suppose fixed cost rises by $200 while the displayed price and profit-maximizing output initially remain unchanged. Relative to the graph, total economic profit becomes:
questions.feedback: The graph implies initial profit of $500; a $200 fixed-cost increase reduces it to $300.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly extracts the firm’s economic profit from the displayed graph?
options: Choose minimum ATC first; multiply that output by the $30 market price to obtain economic profit
Use AVC = $10 as profit per unit; multiply $10 by Q = 50 to obtain total profit
Use rising-MC P = MC to get Q = 50; read ATC = $20; compute ($30 − $20) × 50
Use market price $30 as profit per unit; multiply it by Q = 50 without subtracting cost
questions.feedback: Competitive-firm analysis chooses Q from P = MC first, then measures P − ATC at that quantity.

questions.q: On the displayed profit graph, which two values must be compared after Q = 50 is chosen to determine profit per unit?
options: Price and AVC
MC and AVC
ATC and AVC
Price and ATC
questions.feedback: Profit per unit is price minus ATC at the chosen output.

questions.q: At what output does the firm operate on the displayed break-even graph?
options: 50 units
25 units
75 units
100 units
questions.feedback: P = MR intersects rising MC at Q = 50.

questions.q: At Q = 50, what relationship holds between price and ATC?
options: P = $15 and ATC = $25
P = ATC = $25
P = $25 and ATC = $15
P exceeds ATC by $10
questions.feedback: The price line passes through ATC at $25.

questions.q: What economic profit does the firm earn at the displayed output?
questions.feedback: Because P equals ATC at Q = 50, economic profit is zero.

questions.q: Using the break-even price and output shown, calculate the firm’s total revenue.
Using the displayed AVC at the chosen output, calculate total variable cost.
What total fixed cost is implied by the displayed ATC and AVC values at Q = 50?
Why is the firm not at its shutdown point on this graph?
options: P lies below minimum AVC, so the firm cannot cover variable cost at the selected output
The firm sets P equal to ATC itself, so the market shutdown rule does not apply here
P equals ATC and remains above AVC, so the firm covers all economic costs rather than shutting down
Zero economic profit always triggers shutdown, even when price remains above average variable cost for the displayed firm
questions.feedback: Zero economic profit is break-even, not shutdown; price remains above AVC.

questions.q: At the selected output, compare price with ATC. Which statement about economic profit is most accurate?
options: The firm necessarily earns zero accounting profit because economic and accounting costs are identical
The firm should shut down because any zero-profit outcome fails to cover average variable cost
The firm bears a loss equal to total fixed cost because price only covers its variable cost
The firm earns zero economic profit while covering the normal return included in economic cost
questions.feedback: Economic cost includes opportunity cost, so zero economic profit is consistent with normal profit.

questions.q: If market price fell slightly below $25 but remained above AVC, with the cost curves unchanged, what would the firm do in the short run?
options: Choose the lower-price rising-MC intersection and operate with a loss as long as price remains above AVC
Shut down immediately because any price below ATC makes short-run production economically irrational for the displayed firm
Keep Q fixed at 50 because price-taking firms never change output when the market price changes
Raise the firm’s own price back to $25 and continue producing at the original break-even output
questions.feedback: A competitive firm continues producing when price covers AVC, even if price is below ATC.

questions.q: What feature of the displayed graph establishes break-even?
options: At the chosen output, market price equals AVC while ATC remains above the price line
At the chosen output, the market price equals ATC while price remains above AVC
MC stays below the market price at every possible output, so profit cannot become negative
ATC falls to zero at the chosen output, so all economic costs have been eliminated
questions.feedback: Break-even occurs where P = ATC at the chosen output.

questions.q: Where does the $30 MR line meet rising MC in the loss-but-operate graph?
options: 20 units
40 units
30 units
60 units
questions.feedback: The horizontal price line meets rising MC at Q = 30.

questions.q: What market price does the firm face?
questions.feedback: The P = MR = AR line is at $30.

questions.q: The blue ATC guide at the chosen 30-unit output lands on which dollar value?
questions.feedback: The ATC guide at Q = 30 is $40.

questions.q: The green AVC marker at Q = 30 gives what variable cost per unit?
questions.feedback: The AVC guide at Q = 30 is $20.

questions.q: At the firm’s chosen output in the loss graph, what is the loss per unit?
options: $20 per unit
$30 per unit
$10 per unit
$40 per unit
questions.feedback: Loss per unit is ATC − P = $40 − $30 = $10.

questions.q: What is the firm’s total economic loss at the selected output?
Using the loss-case price and selected output, calculate the firm’s total revenue.
Use the vertical gap between ATC and AVC at the chosen output to calculate total fixed cost.
Why does operating at Q = 30 reduce the firm’s short-run loss relative to shutting down?
options: Revenue falls below total variable cost, so operating increases the loss relative to shutdown
Producing eliminates the firm’s fixed cost, so its remaining loss consists only of variable cost
Revenue covers all variable cost and contributes $300 toward the firm’s fixed cost
The firm can charge above the market price, so production restores the lost $300 automatically
questions.feedback: At Q = 30, revenue is $900 and TVC is $600, leaving $300 to cover fixed cost.

questions.q: If the firm shut down instead of producing at Q = 30, what short-run loss would it bear based on the graph?
questions.feedback: Shutdown avoids variable cost but leaves the $600 fixed cost.

questions.q: Trace the firm’s short-run and long-run logic from the loss graph. Which sequence is valid?
options: Choose Q = 30 where P = MC; because AVC < P < ATC, operate with a $300 loss and face exit pressure if it persists
Choose minimum ATC; because P equals ATC there, operate with zero profit and no exit pressure for the displayed firm
Shut down at Q = 0; because P < ATC, avoid all variable and fixed costs immediately
Raise price to $40; keep Q = 30 and convert the displayed loss into economic profit
questions.feedback: The firm covers variable cost but not total cost, so it operates in the short run and may exit in the long run.

questions.q: Checkpoint: Compare the firm’s operating loss with the fixed cost implied by the graph. What does that comparison tell the firm?
options: Shutting down reduces the short-run loss below the firm’s unavoidable fixed cost
Producing reduces the short-run loss relative to shutting down
Raising price to average total cost eliminates the loss in a competitive market
Producing creates economic profit because revenue exceeds variable cost
questions.feedback: Operating loses $300, while shutdown would leave the $600 fixed cost.

questions.q: What price is shown by the horizontal P = MR = AR line?
questions.feedback: The horizontal price line is at $10.

questions.q: Which labeled point marks the minimum of AVC?
options: Point B
Point C
Point D
Point A
questions.feedback: MC crosses AVC at its minimum at point A.

questions.q: Given the displayed price, what is the firm’s short-run output?
options: 0 units
22 units
44 units
50 units
questions.feedback: The $10 price lies below minimum AVC, so the firm shuts down and supplies zero.

questions.q: What is the firm’s shutdown price on the displayed graph?
questions.feedback: Minimum AVC is $20 at point A.

questions.q: Where does the firm’s short-run supply curve begin?
options: At the left end of the entire MC curve
At point C and then along ATC
At point A and then along rising MC
Along the AVC curve below A
questions.feedback: Short-run supply is rising MC at and above minimum AVC.

questions.q: Suppose market price rose to the price level represented by point B. Which output rule would apply?
options: Continue producing zero because the original $10 price permanently determines the firm’s short-run output
Produce at point A because minimum AVC fixes the firm’s output whenever market price changes
Choose point C because minimum ATC determines output even when marginal revenue intersects MC elsewhere
Produce at point B because its rising-MC value equals the new price and lies above the shutdown threshold
questions.feedback: Once price is above minimum AVC, the firm chooses the rising-MC intersection.

questions.q: What economic role does point C play on the graph?
options: Point C is minimum ATC, where the rising MC curve crosses the ATC curve
Point C is minimum AVC, where rising MC first enters the firm’s short-run supply curve
Point C is the current market price, where the horizontal P = MR line crosses MC
Point C is the shutdown point, where price exactly equals the minimum of average variable cost
questions.feedback: MC crosses ATC at ATC’s minimum at point C.

questions.q: Why is the rising MC segment below point A excluded from the firm’s short-run supply curve?
options: MC stops being a valid marginal-cost curve below point A, so the firm cannot use that portion
Prices on that MC segment are below minimum AVC, so production would not cover the firm’s variable cost
ATC lies below AVC on that segment, so fixed cost becomes negative and supply must begin later for the displayed firm
The firm becomes a price setter below point A, so its marginal cost no longer guides output
questions.feedback: A competitive firm supplies zero when price is below minimum AVC.

questions.q: If the firm’s fixed cost fell while MC and AVC remained exactly as drawn, what would happen to the shutdown price?
options: It would fall to $10
It would rise to $30
It would remain $20
It would become equal to minimum ATC
questions.feedback: Shutdown depends on AVC, not fixed cost; minimum AVC remains $20.

questions.q: The $10 price line can intersect MC at a low-output portion of the curve. Why is that intersection not the firm’s chosen output?
options: The firm must always choose the highest feasible output, so any low-output MC crossing is irrelevant
ATC must fall to zero before a firm can produce, so the low-output crossing cannot be used
A competitive firm ignores marginal cost at low output and chooses quantity from average total cost instead
P is below minimum AVC, so the shutdown condition rules out the low-output P = MC crossing
questions.feedback: P = MC is not sufficient; the chosen point must also satisfy the shutdown condition and lie on rising MC.

questions.q: If price were exactly $20 at point A, which statement would be correct?
options: The firm is indifferent between producing at the shutdown output and shutting down in the short run
The firm earns positive economic profit because price equals the minimum of average variable cost for the displayed firm
The firm must exit immediately because reaching minimum AVC makes long-run production impossible
The firm instead produces at point C because ATC determines the short-run shutdown quantity
questions.feedback: At minimum AVC, revenue exactly covers variable cost, making the firm indifferent in the short run.

questions.q: Which labeled point anchors the lower end of the competitive firm’s short-run supply curve?
options: Point B
Point A
Point C
Point D
questions.feedback: Supply begins where rising MC crosses minimum AVC, point A.

questions.q: Read the intersection of market S and D in the paired profit case. What price clears the market?
questions.feedback: Market supply and demand intersect at a price of $40.

questions.q: The market panel settles at $40. Reading across to the firm panel, which quantity is selected where MR meets rising MC?
options: 40 units
75 units
100 units
90 units
questions.feedback: On the firm panel, P = MR = $40 meets rising MC at Q = 90.

questions.q: At the 90-unit output in the paired profit graph, what vertical price–ATC gap represents profit per unit?
options: $20 per unit
$5 per unit
$15 per unit
$40 per unit
questions.feedback: Price is $40 and ATC is $20, so profit per unit is $20.

questions.q: What is total economic profit for the representative firm?
How does the market-panel equilibrium price enter the representative firm’s decision?
options: It becomes the firm’s ATC curve, determining average cost at every possible output level
It becomes the firm’s quantity of 75, so market quantity and individual output are identical
It becomes the firm’s horizontal P = MR = AR line used to choose output along MC
It shifts the firm’s MC curve upward, changing production cost without changing marginal revenue
questions.feedback: A price-taking firm accepts the market price as its marginal and average revenue.

questions.q: Using the market price and representative firm output in the paired profit graph, calculate total revenue.
At Q = 90, use the displayed ATC to calculate the representative firm’s total cost.
The firm panel shows positive economic profit. If that condition persists, which market adjustment follows?
options: Persistent profit induces exit, shifting market supply left and pushing the equilibrium price upward for the displayed firm
Persistent profit induces entry, shifting market supply right and pushing the equilibrium price downward
The representative firm raises its own price, so market supply stays fixed while profit disappears
Market demand becomes horizontal, so entry changes firm output without affecting the market price
questions.feedback: Positive economic profit attracts entry, increasing market supply.

questions.q: Trace the representative firm’s output choice as entry lowers the market price while its cost curves stay fixed. What happens to output?
options: It remains fixed at 90 because firms are price takers
It rises because lower price increases demand for the firm
It moves down along rising MC to a lower quantity
It becomes equal to market quantity
questions.feedback: A lower horizontal MR line meets rising MC at a lower firm output.

questions.q: Why can the market quantity of 75 thousand not simply be used as the representative firm’s output?
options: The representative firm must always produce more than the entire market whenever it earns positive profit for the displayed firm
The market quantity is actually an average-cost value, so it cannot be compared with firm output
Price-taking firms do not choose output, so the right-panel quantity has no role in the analysis
The panels describe different aggregation levels and use separate quantity scales for market and firm output
questions.feedback: The left panel is the entire market; the right panel is one representative firm.

questions.q: Which chain correctly describes the adjustment implied by the two panels?
options: Market sets P = $40; firm chooses Q = 90; profit attracts entry; supply rises; price and firm output fall
Firm chooses P = $40; market adopts Q = 90; losses cause exit; supply rises and price falls
Market sets Q = 90 for every firm; entry occurs but leaves both market price and firm output unchanged for the displayed firm
Firm chooses minimum AVC; entry shifts market demand right and raises both price and individual output
questions.feedback: The market determines price, the firm chooses output, and persistent profit triggers entry and lower price.

questions.q: Using the displayed ATC and AVC at Q = 90, what total fixed cost is implied for the representative firm?
Start with the market panel. Which sequence correctly determines the representative firm’s current outcome?
options: Read market Q = 75; use it as firm output; then compare the market quantity with the firm AVC curve
Choose minimum ATC on the firm panel first; then use that cost to determine the market equilibrium price
Read market P = $40; use it as firm MR; choose Q = 90 where MR = MC; then compare P with ATC
Let the firm choose P = $40 first; then shift market demand until market quantity equals firm output
questions.feedback: The market establishes price; the firm uses that price to choose its own output and evaluate profit.

questions.q: Checkpoint: If the profit shown in the firm panel persists, what completes the long-run adjustment?
options: Persistent profit causes exit, reducing market supply until the market price falls below AVC
The firm raises its own price, shifting ATC downward until economic profit disappears without entry
Market demand becomes perfectly elastic, preventing changes in price as new firms enter the industry for the displayed firm
Persistent profit attracts entry, increasing market supply until economic profit is driven toward zero
questions.feedback: Persistent positive economic profit attracts entry and erodes the profit.

questions.q: In the paired loss case, what price is transmitted from the market equilibrium to the representative firm?
questions.feedback: Market supply and demand intersect at $15.

questions.q: With the market equilibrium price at $15, where does the firm panel place the MR–MC output choice?
options: 15 units
50 units
75 units
100 units
questions.feedback: The firm’s P = MR line meets rising MC at Q = 50.

questions.q: Use the price and ATC at the representative firm’s chosen output. What is the loss per unit?
options: $5 per unit
$8 per unit
$3 per unit
$15 per unit
questions.feedback: ATC is $18 and price is $15, so loss per unit is $3.

questions.q: What is the representative firm’s total economic loss?
Use price and AVC at the chosen output. Why does the representative firm continue producing in the short run?
options: P = $15 exceeds AVC = $10 at Q = 50, so revenue covers variable cost and part of fixed cost
P = $15 exceeds ATC = $18 at Q = 50, so the firm is earning positive economic profit
The competitive firm can raise its own price above $15, so it avoids the loss shown by ATC
Producing at Q = 50 eliminates fixed cost, so any price above AVC guarantees zero economic loss
questions.feedback: The firm covers variable cost and part of fixed cost because P > AVC.

questions.q: At Q = 50 in the loss-making firm panel, use price to calculate total revenue.
From the ATC–AVC separation in the loss panel, determine the firm’s total fixed cost.
The firm panel shows an economic loss. If that loss persists, which market adjustment follows?
options: Persistent losses induce entry, shifting market supply right and lowering the market price further
The representative firm raises its own price, leaving market supply and the number of firms unchanged
Market demand becomes horizontal, allowing every remaining firm to choose a higher price independently
Persistent losses induce exit, shifting market supply left and raising the market price for survivors
questions.feedback: Persistent losses induce firms to exit, reducing market supply.

questions.q: Trace the surviving firm’s output choice as exit raises market price while its cost curves stay fixed. What happens to output?
options: It rises along the firm’s rising MC curve
It falls because the market has fewer firms
It stays at 50 regardless of price
It becomes equal to total market output
questions.feedback: A higher horizontal MR line intersects rising MC at a larger firm quantity.

questions.q: How much does producing at Q = 50 contribute toward covering fixed cost?
questions.feedback: Contribution is (P − AVC) × Q = ($15 − $10) × 50 = $250.

questions.q: Why should the market quantity of 75 thousand not be divided by the firm quantity of 50 to infer an exact number of firms from this graph alone?
options: The firm quantity is a price measure, so dividing market quantity by it would mix incompatible variables
Competitive market quantity cannot be measured, so the left-panel quantity has no usable economic meaning for the displayed firm
The panels do not establish enough about firm counts, identical outputs, and compatible quantity units for that calculation
The market panel lacks an equilibrium, so its quantity cannot be compared with any firm-level outcome
questions.feedback: The graph links price across panels but does not supply enough information to infer an exact firm count.

questions.q: Trace the paired market-and-firm loss case through long-run adjustment. Which sequence is valid?
options: Market sets P = $15; firm shuts down because P < ATC; persistent shutdown attracts entry and lowers price for the displayed firm
Firm sets P = $15; market adopts Q = 50; persistent profit causes entry and higher market supply
Market sets firm ATC at $18; firm shifts market demand left until price equals average cost
Market sets P = $15; firm chooses Q = 50; AVC < P < ATC creates a loss; persistent loss causes exit and higher price
questions.feedback: The firm operates in the short run because P > AVC, but persistent loss creates exit pressure.

questions.q: Compare operating with shutting down using the displayed values. Which statement is correct?
options: Operating loses $150 versus $400 if shut down, so operating reduces the loss by $250
Operating and shutdown each lose $400, so the output decision does not affect the loss
Shutdown loses $150 versus $400 while operating, so shutdown reduces the loss by $250
Operating earns $250 of economic profit while shutdown produces a $400 economic loss
questions.feedback: The $250 contribution toward fixed cost reduces the loss from $400 to $150.

questions.q: Checkpoint: Use the market price, ATC, and AVC at the chosen output. What is the correct combined short-run and long-run decision?
options: Shut down immediately because P < ATC; doing so eliminates both fixed and variable costs
Operate with a short-run loss because P > AVC; persistent losses create long-run exit pressure
Earn positive profit because P > AVC; persistent profit therefore attracts long-run entry for the displayed firm
Raise price from $15 to $18; a competitive firm can restore break-even by changing price
questions.feedback: P > AVC supports short-run production, but P < ATC creates a loss and possible long-run exit.

questions.q: In the market panel where equilibrium quantity is 100, what equilibrium price is shown?
questions.feedback: Market supply and demand intersect at $25.

questions.q: At the long-run market price of $25, which firm quantity lies at the rising-MC intersection?
options: 25 units
75 units
100 units
50 units
questions.feedback: The firm’s horizontal MR line meets MC at Q = 50.

questions.q: What economic profit does the representative firm earn at the displayed long-run equilibrium?
questions.feedback: Price equals ATC at the selected output, so economic profit is zero.

questions.q: Which pair of conditions holds at the representative firm’s selected output?
options: P < AVC and MC < ATC for the displayed firm
P = MC and P = minimum ATC
P > ATC and MC < AVC
P = AVC and ATC = 0
questions.feedback: Long-run competitive equilibrium has P = MC and P at minimum ATC.

questions.q: At the selected output, which efficiency condition is illustrated by the equality of price and marginal cost?
options: Product differentiation
Shutdown efficiency
Allocative efficiency
Market power
questions.feedback: P = MC is the competitive allocative-efficiency condition.

questions.q: At the selected output, which efficiency condition is illustrated by production at the minimum of ATC?
options: Allocative inefficiency
Price discrimination
Strategic interdependence
Productive efficiency
questions.feedback: Producing at minimum ATC is productive efficiency.

questions.q: If demand and cost conditions remain unchanged, what entry-or-exit pressure exists at the displayed equilibrium?
options: Neither entry nor exit pressure
Strong entry pressure only
Strong exit pressure only
Both entry and exit simultaneously
questions.feedback: Zero economic profit removes the incentive for net entry or exit.

questions.q: How should the two panels be linked analytically?
options: Firm Q = 50 determines the market quantity; the market then adjusts price to match firm output
Market supply and demand set $25; the firm takes $25 as MR and chooses Q = 50
The firm chooses $25 first; market demand then shifts until the chosen price clears the market
Market quantity directly determines the firm’s ATC; the firm then produces at that average cost
questions.feedback: The market sets price; the representative price-taking firm uses it as P = MR = AR.

questions.q: Why does the graph represent a long-run competitive benchmark rather than merely a short-run break-even point?
options: P is below AVC, so the firm shuts down and exit pressure immediately develops for the displayed firm
P exceeds ATC, so positive profit attracts new firms into the market
P = MC = minimum ATC, economic profit is zero, and no net entry or exit pressure remains
P equals AVC below ATC, so the firm operates with a continuing economic loss
questions.feedback: The conjunction of zero economic profit, minimum ATC, and P = MC characterizes the long-run benchmark.

questions.q: Which statement best summarizes the two-panel long-run equilibrium?
options: Firm sets P = $25; firm chooses Q = 50 where price exceeds ATC and positive profit persists
Market sets P = $25; firm shuts down at Q = 0 because price equals its average total cost
Market and firm quantities must match exactly because all competitive firms face the same market price
Market sets P = $25; firm chooses Q = 50 where P = MC = minimum ATC and economic profit is zero
questions.feedback: Competitive long-run equilibrium combines market price-taking, zero economic profit, and efficient firm output.
